utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have today's appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner, assisted by Crispian Smith, case manager, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, and Eugene O'Sullivan appearing for the Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For Zupljanin Defence this morning, Igor Pantelic and Dragan Krgovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just raise two matters. The first is this: Your Honours should have seen the list that has been sent by the Prosecution for the -- not the next witness, but the one after. If you look at the list, you'll see that some of the documents there are the subject of two outstanding motions, one February the 18th and the other March -- I can't remember the date now, but Your Honours asked the Defence to put in an oral expedited response today, I believe. But we'd be grateful if we could certainly have a ruling on the February one as soon as possible. Your Honour, the other matter is this, can I just mention this? As you will have realised, I was slightly surprised on Friday when I heard that not all the intercepts were to be admitted. The problem that is raised by this is the following: We assumed, from the written rulings we got in respect of the 92 ter, that except where specifically indicated, the documents would be admitted as part of the 92 package. I see Judge Delvoie shaking his head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: These weren't 92 ter package, Ms. Korner, the intercepts we are -- you know now which ones are concerned. They weren't on the 92 ter package list; they were on the other list, the list of new documents for that witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, then, Your Honours, in that case, the point that I'm about to make I hadn't appreciated, because although we got the four intercepts to which this related from Mr. Dygeus on Friday night, late, I hadn't realised they were separate from the 92 ter package. In that case, I won't pursue this part of my point any further. Oh, and sorry, Your Honour, the motion that is March the 17th, the second motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So would the Usher kindly escort the witness back to the stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the meantime, Your Honours, I do apologise, I missed my -- our learned friend and colleague Mr. Miroslav Cuskic is this morning with us. Sometimes it's difficult, you know, in Monday morning to count everyone and to see what's going on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, good morning to you, sir. Mr. Krgovic is about to continue his cross-examination. I would remind you that you're still on your oath. Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning, Mr. Tutus.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us continue where we left off on Friday. We were talking about the jurisdictions of the public security stations and the Security Services Centre. I would like to show you tab 4 in the Prosecution's binder. They showed it to you earlier. It's Exhibit P1015.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You are certainly aware that sometime in June there occurred a change in jurisdictions, that is, an amendment of the Law on Courts, so that certain offences which used to be within the competence of the higher courts were assigned thereby to lower courts?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And, accordingly, you received a letter from Mr. Zupljanin, the one you are looking at now.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And this change in jurisdiction, which should follow the rules on the internal organisation of the MUP, created certain problems for your station because you did not have enough personnel or enough resources to cover also this workload which was shifted to lower courts by this change; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understood your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Look at the next document, please. It's tab 5, 65 ter 2376. It's your reply to this letter sent by Mr. Zupljanin. In this reply, you say precisely what I've just described. For objective reasons, you believe that the Public Security Station will have certain difficulty in handling the new workload.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my answer, I indicate the procedure regarding jurisdiction between CSB and the station, and certainly this directive from the centre added to the workload of the Public Security Station Banja Luka, whereas there was no increase of personnel, and certainly that could play a role.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you say, towards the bottom of this document: "For these reasons, we have so far several times suggested an expansion of the job specification in the Department for the Prevention and Detection of Crime," with no result?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then you suggest that a new number of jobs be created for you to be able to handle the new workload. That's the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that after a while, because this issue did not relate only to the Public Security Station Banja Luka, Vlado Kusmuk came to visit from the MUP, and in the process of supervision and inspection, he was trying to deal with this problem, and ultimately this whole issue of jurisdiction was resolved differently?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the visit of Mr. Kusmuk, but I don't know about these details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please look at the last page of the document. It's your signature?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in that case I would like to ask for an exhibit number for this document. I have no indication if it's been admitted already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It is, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, could you please look at the next exhibit, number 6, P1078.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In your evidence, you spoke a lot about these various dispatches that had been sent. I would like you to look at the second page of this document, dated 2nd March 1992, the last paragraph, 11, where Stojan Zupljanin says: "I warn you once again that you have obligations established by the instruction on urgent, current and interim reporting on all security-related events."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please slow down and repeat what he said after quoting the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I have to slow down for the transcript because the interpreters cannot follow what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In my opinion, as I was saying, this is probably the result of the fact that new people came to the Public Security Station without any experience in police work.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. There was a large number of people who came from civilian jobs, along party lines, and a large number of them had nothing -- no knowledge, no skills, in the service.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's entirely my fault, but could I -- Mr. Krgovic said, Look at 6. Does he mean tab 6 in the Prosecution documents, in the Zupljanin documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's in my tab 6, and it's P1078.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I know that, but it's not -- do you mean tab 6 in the documents you prepared?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Look at this paragraph 10, please, mentioning an incident which is another proof that police officers are failing to comply with the obligations imposed by our previous dispatches. Mr. Tutus, do you remember there were problems in the system of reporting, execution of orders from the centre indicated in the dispatches, and that was discussed at the expanded collegium of the centre?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At various meetings of the Professional Council of the centre, every time we met these problems of mutual reporting were always discussed. But as far as execution of orders from the ministry is concerned, I don't think there were any problems there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Primarily because you, yourself, had ample experience and you spent your entire career until then on the police force, so you were very skilled in all these matters of reporting and execution of decisions, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that didn't depend on me alone. It depended also on my associates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now look at the next exhibit, tab 7, 1D137, page 1. The Prosecutor asked you earlier about the substance of this document. I would just like you to look to whom this was addressed. In addition to the CSB, it was sent to the Ministry of Interior in the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and to the MUP of the SRBH, to the minister, deputy minister for information, and to the CSBs in Bihac, Livno, and Doboj, also for information, to the chief. Is it the case that in April, such documents were forwarded to CSBs for their information?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Would you now look at the next exhibit, your tab 8, and it's P355. The Prosecutor questioned you on this document earlier, and I would like you to read, under the subheading "Conclusions," the first paragraph, where we can see the reasons and the introduction into all these events. It says there are problems that occurred regarding the future state organisation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the fundamental principles of which were established by the Sarajevo Agreement and confirmed by the Brussels recognition of Bosnia and Herzegovina within its existing borders, where the coexistence of the constituent peoples can only be defined through three constitutive units. And it says, in view of the international situation and the agreement among the three parties, in order to establish three entities, all these conclusions are made in keeping with an agreement that had been reached among all the three constituent parties in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to follow from this, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now move to page 2 and look at the last paragraph but one. Basically, these are conclusions adopted by the council. It says: "After the discussion involving almost everyone, these conclusions were adopted unanimously ..." It follows that certain conclusions were proposed and then were unanimously adopted by everyone present?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Look at the next page, paragraph 2. By that time, Republika Srpska had already been established, and the MUP of Republika Srpska. All employees in the CSB Banja Luka who were employed as of 1st April 1992, in keeping with Article 27 on the Law on Internal Affairs, all of them are taken over by the Ministry of the Interior of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And look at the next page, paragraph 7, where the conclusions say: "In view of the new situation, until such time as the status of the constituent entities of the other two peoples in the BH Republic is solved, the Banja Luka CSB will, in the future, receive instructions exclusively from the CSB chief, without interrupting the current traffic of dispatches with the MUP." It says, basically, that links with the MUP of the SRB need not be interrupted, and it's in keeping with the previous document which says it needs to be forwarded to the MUP of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Just a correction. When I said that communication would not be interrupted, I was referring to the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On the next page, look at conclusion number 18, where the heading on documents is mentioned. And now it's to contain the words "Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Ministry of the Interior, Sarajevo Security Services Centre, Banja Luka." And that was the heading you used from that point onwards in your internal communication; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the letterhead, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And now look at item 22, where it says that: "All management-level employees shall inform their employees in detail of the reasons and need for this reorganisation. It is in our interest to preserve the ethnic representation of SJB employees in proportion to the ethnic structure of the population in the municipalities." This is precisely what you did when you convened that meeting and explained to your men what was going on and asked the Croats and Muslims to stay; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: From these conclusions, we can see that at least in the Banja Luka centre, the change was not towards MUP consisting of employees of only one ethnicity; on the contrary?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anyone who wanted to stay and work was able to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the next document, P367. It's number 9 in your binder, tab 9. This is another session of the council of the centre. And when summing up the discussion, the chief, Stojan Zupljanin, proposed the following conclusions. So this is the same format that we saw in the previous meeting. So please look at conclusion number 4, which refers to orders. Evidently, there is a certain problem in carrying out the decisions of the centre - I'm not referring to your station, but others - because he repeats over and over again that his orders and instructions should be complied with. And here he goes even further and says: "All my orders conveyed orally as well as those I may forward by dispatch must be carried out." So it's evident from this that orders and decisions were not being carried out, especially after the war broke out. I'm not saying this refers to your particular public security station.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At these meetings of the Professional Collegium, one could reach the conclusion that such problems did occur in some public security stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And in item 12, we see here that the delivery of monthly reports is specially highlighted, and the chiefs who are not submitting these reports are told that 10 per cent of their salary will be deducted. So obviously this problem also existed in the public security stations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please now look at conclusion 23. The Prosecutor read this conclusion to you, but only the first sentence, where it says: "In your activities, you are duty-bound to comply with all measures and actions ordered by the Crisis Staff." Could you read the rest of this paragraph with regard to disarmament. So this refers to the issue of disarmament, does it not? That's what this paragraph is about, isn't it, that these dead-lines should be complied with?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see this. In paragraph 23, it says: "In all our activities, we are obliged to observe all measures and apply all procedures ordered by the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region." And then in the next paragraph, it's correct that on a general level, insisting on the disarmament of extremist groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So the measures that are to be observed relate to disarmament?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one could make that connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, I'll show you another document now. It's number 10, tab number 10, and it's P160. So please go to page 6, ERN number 0324-1856, and it's page 9 of the English version. It's Stojan Zupljanin's intervention at the meeting in Belgrade, and this is where he talks about the change in jurisdiction in line with the changes in the law. So he proposes to the minister that the instruction to implement the Law on Internal Affairs be annulled. So this problem did not refer only to Banja Luka, it was a general problem on the territory of Republika Srpska; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, obviously this problem was discussed at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony, when answering the Prosecutor's questions, you mentioned an incident when Stojan Zupljanin criticised Simo Drljaca because of some things that were happening in Prijedor. Do you remember speaking about that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, you were asked when this happened. The Prosecutor suggested it might have been in August, but you were unsure of the time. You only knew it was in summer; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, now please look at page 5. In English, it's page 8. Here, Stojan Zupljanin says that the army, the crisis staffs, should leave such non-defined camps to the Internal Affairs. The conditions in these camps are poor. There is no food. Some individuals do not comply with international standards, they are not appropriate. So Stojan Zupljanin is referring to this problem at the collegium meeting, and informing all those present and the minister that there are problems in this respect; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I see this as a response to the information he received because of which he criticised Simo Drljaca.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's possible that this is connected to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 4, he also talks about some problems in the work of the centre where the army is asking for police officers to be engaged in combat and pushing them onto the front-lines. Do you remember this being discussed at the collegium?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please look at page 6. You spoke about this in your testimony, where Mr. Zupljanin says that the military courts are not functioning, that the judges have not been appointed, and so on. This is another problem that occurred in the work of the centre, and you spoke about it, did you not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were problems in the functioning of the military courts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph, it says that several thousand court cases remain unfinished. There are no criminal judges. Judges are intimidated. They're being threatened. In some municipalities, hardened criminals are being released from prison. All this is affecting the rule of law, the work of the police. So all of these were problems in the work of the centre at that time, were they not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, can I just put in a small question here? The expansion of jurisdiction that you told us about earlier this morning, what was that really about? Which new crimes or areas were transferred from the higher judicial levels to the local courts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The passing of the new Law on the Courts, and in this dispatch of the chief of the centre, the crimes of murder, robbery - there were a lot of those - were put under the jurisdiction of the stations, which would be a great burden for us. Previously, these crimes had been within the competency of the centre. In our internal documents, it said that public security stations are immediately tasked with dealing with crimes that the lower courts dealt with, whereas the centre would deal with crimes that the higher courts dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But did the expanded jurisdiction cover also the military courts or was it only these ordinary civilian criminal courts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only civil courts, not the military.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Right. So am I right to understand that the expansion of the jurisdiction over serious offences, such as murder and robberies, did not affect the military courts? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, please look at page 20 now, where we see the conclusions. Evidently, certain conclusions were reached at this meeting. This was how such meetings were conducted: There would be a discussion, problems would be put forward, and then some conclusions would be reached, and persons would be tasked with dealing with certain problems.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the centre?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Professional Council of the centre was an advisory body to the chief of the centre. After every discussion, the chief would draw a conclusion and issue tasks. So these tasks enumerated at the end were tasks assigned to individuals by the centre chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, now look at the conclusions here. First, it says that the rules that you mentioned would be changed, and the Administration for Legal, Administrative, and Human Resources would be responsible for that.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now go to page 23/24. It's 23 in B/C/S and 24 in English. And look at conclusion number 7. This is about the prevention and detection of other criminal offences and their perpetrators, looting, war profiteering, serious criminal offences aimed at life and limb, and other criminal offences, regardless of the perpetrators. These are the priorities. And it says here that the ministry and those attending the meeting said that these would be priorities, regardless of the ethnicity of the perpetrator; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And it says: "If objective circumstances render the taking of measures impossible due to the possibility of wider and bigger conflicts with the perpetrators, then evidence and documentation are to be compiled, and the MUP is to be informed on a regular basis." So as I understand this conclusion, on the territory of Republika Srpska crimes were committed by members of military and paramilitary formations and certain people in uniform. For the MUP to be able to implement the law, these criminal offences had to be documented so that when the conditions were put in place, the perpetrators could be brought to justice, and this was to avoid the casualties.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one might say that was the case, so that the traces and the evidence would have to be recorded and preserved as far as was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the next document, tab 11, Exhibit 2D25. It is a letter. The date is 20th, but seems to be corrected to 30th, sent apparently to all public security stations, to the chief, to the commands of the 1st and 2nd Krajina Corps, to the MUP of the SRBH, and the operative duty officer. Have you received this document, have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: There is a link with that conclusion that we discussed. It's on page 5, conclusion number 10. It says: "Reports, facts, and evidence that have been documented shall be delivered, after consulting the centre, to the competent public prosecutors, together with criminal reports," underlined, "against employees of public security stations. And in cases where the public prosecutors are inactive, deliver criminal reports and evidence directly to the senior public prosecutor or the nearest public prosecutor." It's obvious that there is an intention to prosecute even police officers, be they from the reserve force or the active-duty force.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can we now go back one page to conclusion 6, which says --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please slow down and wait for the page to appear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. It's easier for me to leaf through the hard copy, but I'll have to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It says: "Public security stations may not, without the approval of the centre, undertake to guard persons arrested by unauthorised persons, because this work is not within the competence of the service." Basically, it means that in keeping with that discussion from the meeting of the 11th of July, public security stations cannot undertake to guard anyone that is brought in or detained by army personnel, without the approval of the centre.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The centre is not mentioned here, but what you say is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 2, it concerns, obviously, problems in operation and in carrying out the orders from the chief. It says: "Public security stations may not receive nor carry out orders, decisions, conclusions, standpoints, et cetera, of crisis or regional staffs or other organs or legal entities, which have not been adopted following the established procedure and delivered in writing to public security stations and which do not relate to the purview and competence of the service or which are not in accordance with the legislation and bylaws." So for the umpteenth time, we see an indication that certain public security stations are executing orders from other bodies, rather than the CSB?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And that was another problem that was discussed at sessions of the collegium?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It probably was, but I can't remember any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: While we are on the subject, look at the next document, 2D26. It's dated 14 August. Chief Zupljanin established the commission that would tour the municipalities and public security stations in Prijedor, Bosanski Novi, and Sanski Most, precisely to deal with these issues. It mentions the number of persons and the procedure of evacuation. Do you know these people on the commission, Vojin Bera, Vaso Skondric, Ranko Mijic, Jugoslav Rodic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the first two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether this commission toured these municipalities? Are you aware, in fact, that they did, and that they did not find anything wrong in the work of these public security stations?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen this document, it was shown to me by the OTP, but I have nothing to say about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, while we're talking about Prijedor, that, in 1992, there was an operative plan to investigate certain crimes committed in Prijedor? It was partially implemented, but it resulted later, in 1993, in the arrest of some 14 persons; Djordje Dosen, Zoran Zigic, nicknamed Ziga, and Dusan Knezevic, also known as Duca, for crimes commited in Prijedor? This action was led by Zivko Bojic, who I believe was assistant chief when this operation was carried out.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember one operation in Prijedor, and I remember some people were arrested there for some sort of crime, but I believe that was in 1994. I cannot remember the exact year, but I think it's 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is it Mr. Krgovic's intention to put to the witness what did or didn't happen to these people or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm trying to, but the witness is not aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: These people were arrested, criminal reports and charges were filed against 16 persons for crimes against Muslims and Croats. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked in Bijeljina at the time. I know that some persons there were arrested and detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, please look at tab 13 in your binder. It's 65 ter 536, page 1 of this document. You see here that Simo Drljaca reports to the CSB Banja Luka that in the area of Prijedor municipality, there are no camps, prisons, or collection centres. All captured persons -- all prisoners who currently have that status are in the Manjaca POW camp. There is a reference mentioned. He is replying to something. Do you see that Simo Drljaca is saying there are no camps in Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, I will now move to another subject that you have covered in your evidence. Both the Prosecutor and Mr. Zecevic questioned you on it. Look at your tab 14. That is the article you've seen before, Exhibit P536.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think either the Prosecutor or my colleague asked you this. These people concerned were mainly reservists of the 5th Corps, perhaps, unless it's already been renamed by that time. It says reservists are waging a private war and putting themselves above the law. This is all about reservists, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you were answering questions from the Prosecution, you mentioned that among these individuals who imposed the blockade were people with criminal records, people who had committed crimes before?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But that doesn't mean, does it, that everyone taking part in the protest and the blockade had criminal records and were responsible for crimes; just some of them?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'll go back -- I'll come back to this subject, but please look at 65 ter 102, your tab 15.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What was the exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P552. I would like this box in the right bottom corner zoomed in on. The heading is "Special detachments to be formed soon." The Prosecutor devoted quite a lot of time to this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The last paragraph in the left column of the box, it's basically a press statement by Stojan Zupljanin. There is a sentence that reads: "As to the Serbian Defence Forces which were placed under the jurisdiction of the Security Services Centre ..." I think this is something that the reporter says. It's not something that was said by Zupljanin. That's how I read this text.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. I cannot comment on journalistic writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The sentence reads: "As to the Serbian Defence Forces/SOS, which were placed under the jurisdiction of the Security Services Centre by the Krajina Assembly decision, Zupljanin said ..." And then what follows is what Zupljanin said. Everything before that is the opinion of the reporter.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then what follows is actually opposite to what the journalist claimed: "Zupljanin said that the large number of these units' members, being reliable and experienced fighters, would be screened for engagement in the special detachment, while the others would be assigned to the reserve police force and the Krajina Territorial Defence." And that's, in fact, what was done. One group of these people were sent for screening for possible engagement in the special detachment.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the chief says. I don't know whether it was really true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: 65 ter 99 would be our next document. I believe it's been exhibited. The Prosecutor has shown to you the first page of this document. Look at paragraph 3: "The detachment shall be composed of members of the active and reserve forces of the police."

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And that, indeed, was the case. Among the personnel of this detachment, there were both reservists and active-duty staff?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Turn to the next page, please, paragraph 4 in the statement of reasons, talking about recruitment. It says some of the candidates are already part of the Special Platoon. There was a special platoon in the CSB. It was called "Police Detachment." And from every public security station, a number of active-duty staff was taken to be recruited into this special detachment.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know some active-duty policemen were involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And your station also was required to send a number of well-trained, younger policemen to join this unit?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It says here that some of the potential candidates used to be in the same units in Zagreb and Sarajevo, and following the necessary vetting, they could be accepted into the active force. Some have the necessary expertise and skills that would allow them to execute successfully any assignments. However, these candidates would have to go through theoretical training, theory training, and to be vetted before being accepted on to the active force of the unit. Item 111 of the draft decision stipulates that the detachment should comprise both active-duty and reserve personnel. This vetting was actually done during their activity. The detachment had to be set up quickly, and this screening was actually done as they went along, in the course of operation. That's what follows from the document?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And according to the next paragraph, those who became reservists, if they met the criteria and conditions, would be transferred to the active strength; that's what it says here?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So that's how it was envisaged, as I understand this document. This was just one stage. It was formed from the reservist and active-duty policemen, and the composition and use of this detachment were to be defined in the process; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what follows from this explanation, statement of reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether this is an exhibit, Your Honours. I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D55, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, please look at this document. [In English] Yes, here it is now. [Interpretation] Look at this document. It's 2D06-0736. It's your tab 17. You spoke about the military and police records, when questioned by my colleague Mr. Zecevic, and personnel records. And what we see here is a personnel record; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The person's name is Slobodan Dubocanin?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned this Dubocanin and said that as he had arrived with these members of the special unit, that you didn't know where he belonged actually. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at page 2 of this document, where it says what military unit he was a member of, it says here that as of the 17th of January he was a sergeant. Then he was a second lieutenant. After that, he was promoted to the rank of lieutenant. And in 1989, he was promoted to the rank of captain. That's right, isn't it? That's what this document says?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see where it says "sergeant." I don't see where it says "captain."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, please look at page 2. You see where it says here "to rank-class," "sergeant," second lieutenant," "lieutenant," "captain."

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I see that now, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now look at page 2 again, where it says where he served. No, I think it's on the next page where -- his war service record, that is. It says here -- you can't -- well, the first line is illegible, but from the 11th of September, 1991, he was in Military Post 7225 in Banja Luka, up to the 11th of September, 1992. And from the 12th of September, 1992, to the 20th of October, 1992, he was in Military Post 7407 in Knezevo. And after that, until 1994, he was back at Military Post 7225 in Banja Luka. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: From this personnel record, it says that this gentleman, Mr. Dubocanin, was a member of the army.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what follows from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the next page here, which was issued in 2010 by the City of Banja Luka, Ministry of Defence, Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may this document be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: First, I don't know where this comes from. It's got a fax -- may I say we weren't given a translation originally, apparently. But it's got a fax number dated the 9th of March of this year, and it comes from something called Bata Komerc [phoen], whatever that may be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can -- this was sent to my office by my investigator, my office in Belgrade. It's a document issued by the Ministry of Defence, and you can see the seal, the federation seal. So it's an official document issued by the Ministry of Defence. We received it by fax from Banja Luka, and it's verified by a notary public as being identical to the original.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What is verified by a notary public for this copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That the copy is identical to the original.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: However, I'd still like to know where it comes from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Ministry of Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the department in Banja Luka, because now there is a single Ministry of Defence with its seat in Sarajevo, and there is the seal of the federation here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: At the moment, I'm quite happy for it to be MFI'd. This witness can't possibly say whether this is an authentic document. He's never seen it before, or doesn't know anything about the contents, or that the contents are actually correct. But I'm happy to have it MFI'd for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, you have reason to question the authenticity of what appears to be the seal of the relevant department?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, no, no. I'm simply saying at this moment -- I asked where it came from, I'm being told where it comes from. I'm simply saying that this witness cannot actually deal with whether the contents are accurate in any way at all. I'm not sure -- all that happened was he looked at the document and it was read to him, and that's the full extent of what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, is it likely that there is another witness who would be able to -- who would be nearer to this document than the present -- the witness presently on the stand?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness spoke of personnel records kept by the police, and these show clearly that if someone was a member either of the special or the regular police, it would be recorded in his personnel record. So I showed him a personnel record of a person that the witness knows, and the witness identified the form, he identified the person. He knows the person and the information in the form. And in my view, this is sufficient to have the document admitted into evidence. However, if the Prosecutor challenges the authenticity of the document, that's a different matter. We shall tender such forms for all members of the special detachment so that one can see what their war assignment was and where they belonged, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The tendered document is admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D56, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I make a request, then? If counsel says that they have all the records of the so-called special police, would they be prepared to hand them over, including Ljuban Ecim and the like?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have submitted the request to the Ministry of Defence to have all these documents delivered to us. This is the first and only one we have received. But as soon as I receive the remaining documents, I will certainly provide them, yes. This is the only one I have to date. I requested it in connection with the question concerning Kotor Varos and Judge Harhoff asking where Slobodan Dubocanin belonged, and that's when we submitted this request. It took us some three months to obtain this document from the Ministry of Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is, then, a matter I need to raise, but I can raise it at the beginning of the next session, in the absence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will now move on to a different topic, so might it be a convenient time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, you had a matter to raise before the witness is returned to the stand?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I needn't trouble you with that, the one I was going to raise, because I've spoken to Mr. Krgovic and I'm now clear on the matters. But the next witness is here. I've also spoken to Mr. Krgovic about the length of time. He's actually going to go into the next session, he tells me. I have some re-examination, so I wonder if we could release the witness to come back tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, I wanted to move to another subject. But before that, I'd like to clarify certain points of police work with you. In response to a question from Mr. Zecevic, you spoke about one category of information, which was intelligence or operative information, and I understood your answer to mean that there are certain information, gained through operative work of the police, that certain persons are responsible for some sort of offence or crime.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are indicia that something illegal has taken place, some offence has been committed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And when the police get such operative information, they proceed to check this information and to investigate?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And if this is a large-scale job, involving a number of perpetrators or offenders, then you make an operative plan of work?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, an operative work plan is usually made when the operation is on a larger scale or when dealing with a group.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you open now tab 25. It's Exhibit 1D198. Let's wait for it to appear in e-court. You discussed this document with my colleague Mr. Zecevic. It's the operative work plan concerning a large group of perpetrators, and it was necessary to draft an operative work plan; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the plan first refers to this operative information collected from citizens or informants, and then follows an evaluation how and when to proceed with an operation?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor also asked you about the crimes committed during the barricades on the 3rd of April, 1992. You said that criminal reports were filed against these persons and it was handled. Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that's how it was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You were unable to remember specific individuals. Therefore, I'd like to ask you to look at this list, robbery committed by uniformed persons. It's in the attachment. It's page 6, in e-court, in English, or 7. Look at the robberies committed by uniformed persons and the date, 3rd April, 3rd April, 3rd April, all the way up to the end of page 2. It's precisely the crimes you spoke about, the crimes committed on the barricades during the blockade. A large number of crimes, all of them on the first page, were committed on the barricades, if you look at the date?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the date, yes. But for now, I cannot claim with certainty where they were committed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In the first column, you will see "Location," where the crime was committed, and it begins with barricade on Vrbanja, on the 3rd and the 4th.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you will see a list of injured parties, a number of Muslims and Serbs. Then move to page 2, and then you will see the barricade at Tunjice and a number of individual locations. Then move to page 3. Again, barricade at Tunjice -- or, sorry, no, Vrbanja, Vrbanja.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: While you're still on that page, look to the right, the next page with handwriting. "Possible perpetrator," it says "Palackovic," the third from the top on the page with handwriting. Look at the last page.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I see from this that, in practice, the CSB, in co-operation with the Public Security Station, identified a large number of persons who seized cars and valuables and money from civilians at the barricades on the 3rd and the 4th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And if we go back to the original document, page 2, item 2, there's a reference to the operation that needs to be undertaken; arrest and disarm the group led by Brano Palackovic.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That's the group that mistreated people at the barricades, robbed them of cars and money and valuables?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along with others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It also mentions a person who robbed cars and goods at the barricade at Tunjice?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and the task is to identify him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That tells me that this service did their job professionally and proceeded to investigate crimes, bring in and arrest these people?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We heard from previous witnesses that in Banja Luka, in that period from end 1991 and in early 1992, there were many cases where explosives were set and houses and businesses were bombed?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Here, on page 3, item G, we see that there is operative information that Vedran Mandic, Nenad Kajkut and another person were responsible for a number of bombings of various businesses?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And if you look at the last paragraph, the service, following this operative information, identified 27 crimes of violating public order by setting explosives. In fact, the service established that this group perpetrated 27 of these crimes. We can read about operative information concerning their movement and their accomplices?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And there is a reference to another group also involved in bombings, led -- or, rather, one of the members is Goran Gataric. I read somewhere that his involvement was actually established only in 1993, that he was arrested.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember specifically, but I think this crime was processed and prosecuted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Another case is also mentioned, the bombing of the Casablanca Cafe. There were two explosions caused by Samir Knezevic, also known as Kinez, Chinaman, a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So after drafting this operative work plan, you proceed to investigate, try to identify offenders and perpetrators, and conduct operations. Both your public security station and the CSB did this work jointly?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we worked together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can we now show 1D01-0184. It's your tab 26. This is a report filed by the CSB. Look at the last page. I don't think it's Zupljanin's signature.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't. It must be one of his associates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It concerns precisely those crimes, but first it discusses the operative work plan. Look at the description of crimes, mentioning Vedran Mandic, Nenad Kajkut, Drasko Mihajlovic. It's the attack on that police station, and they got killed in the shooting that resulted from the attempt to arrest them.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is all one document. Look through all the pages. This document discusses the activities of this group, and all the attachments are an integral part of this report to the Public Prosecutor's Office?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And on the next page, we see the record of the verbal criminal complaint. This was received on the 7th of May, 1992, in your public security station by the authorised officer, Zdravko Ruzevic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: He was employed in your public security station?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as an operative officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now please go back to the previous page, the first page of the document. There is a note in longhand. It says: "Why did we have to wait so long for this report, I can't understand," and the initials of Stojan Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, he admonishes his workers, his underlings, for taking so long to deal with this case?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's asking for an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to page 3 of the document in English, the record of receipt. It's a criminal complaint received at your station concerning the vehicles that are the subject of your investigation?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And as a result, the CSB also gets involved, and they also provide a report. It's English page 5. Authorised Officer Milorad Jelisavac, employee of the Security Services Centre, signed this one. And the next document is from your public security station, a receipt confirming that something had been given back to that person whose vehicle was seized?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which document do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Certificate on the return of objects.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's from the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now look at the next document. It's the Majdan Police Station, page 7. And page 4, it was drawn up by Petar Tanazovic, was it not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: An employee of your public security station?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the commander of the Majdan Police Station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the next document, well, this is an Official Note drawn up or compiled on the premises of the Majdan Police Station, and it was Ilija Cibic, an employee of yours, who compiled it, was it not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The next document, English page 12, is a report concerning an explosion where a hand-grenade was shown on a shop called Carmen. It was signed by Marinko Bilic and Damir Gunic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: They were employees of your public security station?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were policemen of the Majdan Police Station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And this policeman, Damir Gunic, judging by his name, I would say he was a Croat or a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he could be a Muslim. Marinko Bilic was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You have another note compiled on the 15th of May, 1992. It's the next document, English page 13, also referring to an explosion. It was an employee of yours, Bosko Kudric, who compiled the note, was it not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name was Bosko Kudra.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, Kudra. Let's look at the next document, then. It's a report sent to the Public Prosecutor's Office, signed by the chief of the centre. Could you look at page 3?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And, in fact, this is a report listing criminal offences perpetrated by these persons who were killed and their group; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And these were mostly explosions, and the property was owned by Muslims, Sehitluci and so on?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And on page 2, we see a reference to a Croat, Franjo?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Gagula.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And on page 3, under 3, another explosion, a coffee bar called Biser, Miro Majdandzic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Majdandzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: He was a Croat, was he not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And under number 4, a dry-cleaner shop owned by Josipa Knapic, a Croat; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Under number 5, a fruit shop owned by a Muslim; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And on the next page, under 6, a beer shop. I don't really know what ethnicity this person would be.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, judging by the last name, the person might be a Serb, but I don't know. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then number 8, a hand-grenade was activated and thrown into the Gril shop owned by Darko Djuric?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then under number 9, these persons threw a hand-grenade onto the Majdan pastry shop owned by Abdulah Emini, who was an ethnic Albanian?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And as far as I was able to see from these documents, as a rule, the police investigated these explosions in Banja Luka in the spring of 1992. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the ones we have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: If we move on, we'll see that in investigating these criminal offences, as this is all one file, the Public Security Station was active and participated in all this. So please look further and you will find an Official Note - it's page 24 in English - compiled on the premises of the Public Security Station Centar.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On the 5th of May, by Ranko Stojnic [phoen], Zoran Blagojevic, and Bratislav Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: These are all employees of your public security station, were they not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know them personally, but I think they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But the note was drawn up on the premises of the police station?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they call it the SJB Centar. It should be the SJB Banja Luka, but Centar Police Station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But you can see by the stamp?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, these are policemen in the Centar Police Station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: After that, there's a part of the document where we see that an investigating judge carried out an on-site investigation, so that the whole file shows that regular procedures were followed. Just look through it and then I'll ask you to outline the procedure. But in general, we can say that the procedure was as follows: Once information arrives that there was an explosion, an Official Note is drawn up. The police go on site and take a statement from the damaged party. Most often, it's a policeman on whose territory the offence occurred?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me, I'll explain. When an explosion occurred, depending on the damage, the police would secure the site. As soon as possible, operative employees and forensic technicians, together with the investigating judge, would carry out an on-site investigation. A record would be drawn up, and the policeman who first arrived on site would compile an Official Note and carry out all the official work, with the control of the operative workers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When the investigation was carried out, a forensic technician would be there?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And this whole file, concerning these criminal offences committed by this group, is the product of joint work by the Public Security Station and the Security Services Centre?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the two services co-operated closely, and there were no problems in co-operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as the witness has identified parts of this document, I wish to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 2D57, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, please look at the next document. It's 1D03-1816, and it's your tab 27. Just let's wait until it comes up on the screen. This document, issued by the Public Security Station in Banja Luka, is signed on page 2, it says, by you, although we don't see the signature.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And it's sent by Zoran Josic, your chief?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the chief of the Crime Prevention Service Department.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, when I showed you the operative work plan at the outset, I read out the name of a person called Samir Nezirevic, known as Kinez, and he was the person who threw hand-grenades on two occasions?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So this is the same person. The operative plan was, in part, carried out by your public security station, was it not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the next page, where it says that an action was launched to capture the persons who participated in these bombings.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It's also a document issued by the Public Security Station?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: After this, this form which is attached, please take a look at it. It is a form of the MUP of the Public Security Station, requiring detailed -- details about the criminal offence. This is all statistical data?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the next -- well, not the next, but the report on arrest, and bringing a person in before the investigating judge, for this person, Samir Nezirevic, it's signed by the chief of the centre, Stojan Zupljanin. Somebody signed it for him, did they not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Djuro Bulic did. He was the chief of the Public Security Services Sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then we have a criminal report filed against this person, again signed by Djuro Bulic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This case of bombing was investigated and dealt with, was it not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this document be given an exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 2D58, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, there's a document here. It's a report on arrest of several persons: Goran Davidovic, Radenko Malic and Zoran Kovacevic. These are all Serbs, are they not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to Goran Davidovic and Radenko Malic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So the criminal offence was carried out against the parish priest, Jure Stipic from Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And somebody signed this for Stojan Zupljanin. So because of the attack on the Catholic parish priest, these persons were taken into custody?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only assume this. I did not have this document before, so I can only tell you what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, look at another document, which is part of this document. It's an Official Note drawn up on the 21st of May on the premises of the Majdan Police Station, and it's, I think -- I do apologise. It's 1D00105 [as interpreted]. I apologise. I know this is a boring exercise, going through these documents. It's 1D00-1105. 28 -- it's tab 28 in your binder page 4 of this document. It's an Official Note compiled by an employee of yours.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to this signature?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Luka Guslov.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was the commander of the police department in Majdan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And from this it follows that Jure Stipic, a Franciscan friar from Stratinska, reported the crime, thus initiating proceedings?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: After this, the Security Services Centre became involved, and there's an Official Note, where these persons were interviewed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And as a result - please go back to page 2 - a criminal report was filed against these persons, was it not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And if you look at page 2 of this criminal report, it says that they were remanded in custody; is that correct? Look at page 2 of the criminal report.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they were remanded in custody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And after this statistical form, it says that these persons also perpetrated other criminal offences. So that after this, let's call it, document, there is another document, English page 45, where the Public Security Station of Banja Luka, your service, compiled an Official Note. It's dated the 13th of April, but this was compiled later. But evidently it's attached to this file because the same persons also perpetrated other crimes?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the note dated the 13th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: If you recall, these persons were mentioned in the operative report as one of the groups known to be committing crimes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What persons are you referring to? Cavic, Dragan Cavic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, Davidovic, Kovacevic, Malic.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wish to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 2D59, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, my colleague asked you about this document before you, but he didn't go into detail as I would like to. You remember, when we were talking about that operative work plan, we mentioned this person. It's your tab 29, and the exhibit number is 1D201, MFI. This is a criminal report against Brane Palackovic, mentioned earlier, and his entire group, 14 of them?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And if you look at the list of crimes for which they were responsible - it's page 7, and in English it's pages 8 and 9 - it's the handwritten number 23. Look at the description of crimes and the dates under 23, 24, 25, 26, and then on the next page, 28, 29, 30, 31. Those are precisely the crimes committed on the barricade on the 3rd of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So again we can agree that the operative work plan adopted at the time was carried out, and criminal reports were filed against these persons for crimes that they committed back then?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were reported. But whether all of them were brought in and whether all of them were remanded in custody, I can't see from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We shall see that later. If you look at this criminal report, you will see what the author says about Brano Palackovic, next to his name, in custody. Look at all persons on the first page. Palackovic, Josic, Racic, Kovacevic, Gajic, according to this document, are in custody?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: 7, Nebojsa Dragojevic, is a fugitive?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Banjac, Tamburic, Sjenica, in custody?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the remaining three are on the run?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now, apart from these crimes I emphasised committed at the barricades, there are other crimes, robbery and theft, mainly against Muslims and Croats, but also against some Serbs?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And if you go further through this document, there will be an Official Note roughly behind page 4. It's a note -- a record from the Public Security Station Banja Luka; English page 19. It's a double-sided copy, the third document after the criminal report, on the left-hand side; English page 19. Have you found it, record of on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It's on the other side, because it's a double-sided copy. I'm not sure you're looking at the right thing, but it seems that my people didn't copy the entire document. You will see a record of on-site investigation, 4th May, made in the Public Security Station Banja Luka. Look at it on the screen. It's dated 2nd May. It's a record of receipt of a verbal criminal report. Remember the question from Judge Hall. This is a form for receiving a verbal criminal report. It's from your public security station, isn't it? Look at the signature, Boro Visic.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The injured party reported this crime. The name of the author of this document is Boro Visic. It's not clear in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It's a question of receipt of a verbal criminal report against these people we've mentioned before, one nicknamed Java, Ivankovic, Palackovic, who stole a car from this person. And then there is a record of on-site investigation; English page 21. The date is 4th April, if you look at the other page of this document. Spasoje Dujakovic is the officer who made the record, and he was an employee in your station, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the next Official Note, English page 23, it's a note drawn up at the Police Station Centar, Banja Luka, pertaining to the same crime committed by Dragan Javorac against Asim Kurjak. It's also about the theft of this car; paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The next page, English page 24, is the record of on-site investigation dated 7 May. Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Also from your public security station?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mario Laks, the injured party, is a Croat, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
